pages.title: Beacons and the MDSMonitor: membership, rank assignment, failover and fencing

features.name: Periodic MDS beacon (MMDSBeacon)
features.description: Dedicated mds-beacon thread sends MMDSBeacon (v8, compat 6) whenever 0.9*mds_beacon_interval has elapsed since the last send; carries gid, name, last-seen MDSMap epoch (PaxosServiceMessage version), want_state, seq, compat, health metrics, mds_features, mds_join_fs, and sys_info only when want_state is up:boot.
features.notes: Hard wire contract with the unmodified mon. mds_beacon_interval is read only in the Beacon constructor.

features.name: Beacon ack handling and MDS-side laggy self-detection
features.description: Acks are matched by seq; RTT measured from the send time; daemon is laggy when no beacon sent within the last mds_beacon_grace seconds was acked (true until the first ack). While laggy the rank defers every incoming message except quiesce-DB peer messages (waiting_for_nolaggy), skips tick upkeep including the health refresh, and after recovery does not mark clients stale for queue_max_age+session_timeout.
features.notes: Self-fencing that bounds the window in which a possibly-replaced MDS still answers clients.

features.name: Heartbeat-gated beacons (internal watchdog)
features.description: Beacon::_send skips sending while the HeartbeatMap is unhealthy; the only worker is the MDSRank handle reset under mds_lock with mds_heartbeat_grace and no suicide grace, so a wedged daemon stops beaconing and the mon fails it over.
features.notes: The mon cannot distinguish a dead daemon from a wedged one; the daemon must suppress its own beacons.

features.name: Boot registration as standby with daemon metadata
features.description: An up:boot beacon from an unknown gid is inserted into FSMap standby_daemons as up:standby with the message source addrs, compat (+INLINE) and join_fscid; sys_info is stored as daemon metadata (mds_metadata/last_metadata). The daemon switches want_state to up:standby when it sees itself in the standby map.
features.notes: Metadata consumed by ceph mds metadata/versions/count-metadata, ceph node ls mds and the mgr.

features.name: Unique daemon name enforcement
features.description: With mds_enforce_unique_name (default true) a boot beacon fails (fail_mds_gid, blocklisting rank holders) every existing daemon with the same name.
features.notes: Restart of a daemon is detected this way when the old gid has not timed out yet.

features.name: File system affinity via mds_join_fs
features.description: The fs field of every beacon is resolved by name to join_fscid; standby selection prefers matching standbys, and the mon replaces lower-affinity actives or standby-replays with better-affinity standbys (one per fs per tick).
features.notes: cephadm sets mds_join_fs=<service_id> via central config.

features.name: Standby selection scoring with host anti-affinity
features.description: get_available_standby filters laggy/frozen/compat-incompatible standbys and scores join_fscid match vs vanilla vs other fs, preferring a different host than the rank's current holder; find_replacement_for prefers the rank's standby-replay.
features.notes: Controlled by fs settings standby_enable_host_anti_affinity and refuse_standby_for_another_fs.

features.name: Rank assignment and initial rank state
features.description: FSMap::promote moves a standby into a fs rank with state up:starting (rank was stopped), up:creating (rank never in) or up:replay (rank failed), sets inc to the FSMap epoch. Driven by MDSMonitor::tick (maybe_promote_standby, maybe_resize_cluster, drop_mds) and fs new.
features.notes: The MDS must implement all three entry paths.

features.name: Standby-replay assignment
features.description: When allow_standby_replay is set and the fs is resizeable, the mon assigns available standbys as up:standby-replay followers of followable ranks; on failure of the active the follower is promoted to up:replay. A follower may only report its state or down:damaged.
features.notes: The daemon cannot refuse the assignment; either implement it (even as an idle follower) or never enable allow_standby_replay.

features.name: Rank state requests via beacon
features.description: request_state sets want_state and sends a beacon immediately: replay->resolve|reconnect, resolve->reconnect, reconnect->rejoin, rejoin->clientreplay|active|stopped, clientreplay->active, creating|starting->active, stopping->stopped. Periodic beacons re-send the request until the map shows it.
features.notes: Clients reconnect when the rank reaches up:reconnect in the MDSMap.

features.name: State transition validation (mon and MDS)
features.description: MDSMap::state_transition_valid is applied by the mon to requested states (invalid -> eviction with blocklist) and by the MDS to assigned states (invalid -> respawn). Standbys may not change state; standby-replay may only go to damaged.
features.notes: Mon checks only the graph, not cluster-wide preconditions.

features.name: Laggy detection and replacement by the mon
features.description: Leader tick marks a daemon laggy after mds_beacon_grace without a noted beacon (deferred up to mds_beacon_mon_down_grace while a mon is down or the quorum is new) and, if the OSDMap is writeable and some MDS beaconed recently, removes laggy standbys/standby-replays and replaces laggy rank holders that have a replacement.
features.notes: Laggy rank holder without replacement stays in the map flagged laggy.

features.name: Fencing of failed rank holders via OSD blocklist
features.description: fail_mds_gid blocklists every address of a rank holder (not standby-replay) until now+mon_mds_blocklist_interval, records the OSDMap epoch as last_failure_osd_epoch, and commits FSMap and OSDMap in one Paxos transaction; the replacement waits for that OSDMap epoch before replay.
features.notes: Needed to keep a single writer of each rank's metadata after failover.

features.name: Self-fencing on removal or blocklist (respawn)
features.description: An MDS that disappears from its MDSMap, sees an invalid transition, or gets -EBLOCKLISTED on a write respawns via execv (new gid, new nonce).
features.notes: A Rust MDS may restart in-process but must re-authenticate (new gid) and rebind with a new nonce.

features.name: Clean shutdown notification (DNE beacon)
features.description: On SIGTERM/SIGINT/asok exit the MDS sends a down:dne beacon and waits up to 1 s for the ack; the mon fails the daemon immediately (blocklisting rank holders) instead of waiting for the grace period.
features.notes: Optional; shortens failover.

features.name: Cluster growth one rank at a time
features.description: When in < max_mds and the fs is joinable and resizeable, each tick promotes one standby to the lowest missing rank (up:creating or up:starting); the next rank waits until the previous one leaves creating/starting.
features.notes: fs set max_mds also clears NOT_JOINABLE.

features.name: Cluster shrink via STOPPING/STOPPED
features.description: When in > max_mds the mon sets the highest active rank to up:stopping; the MDS exports all subtrees (evicting all clients if it is the last rank), drains the purge queue and requests down:stopped; the mon then moves the rank to stopped, removes the daemon and its standby-replays and replies with a null map.
features.notes: Only one rank can be stopping at a time; fs set down true stops all ranks one by one.

features.name: DAMAGED rank reporting and repair
features.description: MDSRank::damaged sends down:damaged (with latest health) and waits mds_mon_shutdown_timeout for the ack while holding mds_lock, then respawns; the mon blocklists the rank holder, fails any follower and moves the rank to damaged until 'mds repaired'.
features.notes: Damaged rank makes clients consider the file system unavailable at mount time.

features.name: Daemon health metrics to cluster health checks
features.description: Each tick the MDS computes MDSHealthMetric entries (TRIM, CLIENT_RECALL, CLIENT_LATE_RELEASE, OLDEST_TID, DAMAGE, READ_ONLY, SLOW_REQUEST, SLOW_METADATA_IO, CACHE_OVERSIZED, CLIENTS_LAGGY, CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH, ESTIMATED_REPLAY_TIME, _MANY summaries); the mon persists them per gid and emits MDS_* health checks with detail lines.
features.notes: Unknown metric ids produce health code '???'. TRIM and CACHE_OVERSIZED gate 'mds fail'/'fs fail' without confirmation.

features.name: FS-level health checks computed by the mon
features.description: MDS_DAMAGE, FS_DEGRADED, MDS_UP_LESS_THAN_MAX, MDS_ALL_DOWN, MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS, FS_INLINE_DATA_DEPRECATED, FS_WITH_FAILED_MDS, MDS_INSUFFICIENT_STANDBY (standby_count_wanted auto-set to 1).
features.notes: Derived purely from map state.

features.name: Export target publication (MMDSLoadTargets)
features.description: Ranks track decaying export-target counters, publish the set to the mon on tick; the mon stores it in mds_info.export_targets; the Migrator waits up to 3 map epochs for a destination to be published; clients open sessions/reconnect to export targets.
features.notes: Only relevant with multiple active ranks.

features.name: Snapshot removal requests (MRemoveSnaps)
features.description: The snap table server sends MRemoveSnaps listing deleted snapids per data pool not yet removed in the OSDMap; the OSDMonitor queues new_removed_snaps and echoes an MRemoveSnaps after commit, which the MDS uses to clear need_to_purge.
features.notes: Requires mon cap 'osd pool rmsnap' (profile mds).

features.name: Client blocklisting via mon command
features.description: evict_client sends {'prefix':'osd blocklist','blocklistop':'add','addr':...} through MonClient, then waits for the latest OSDMap and raises the OSD epoch barrier before killing the session; the command's return code is ignored.
features.notes: Fencing of clients whose capabilities are forcibly revoked.

features.name: allow_multimds_snaps flag set by the MDS
features.description: When all snapshots are post-mimic, the snap table server sends 'fs set <fs> allow_multimds_snaps true' with confirm '--yes-i-am-really-a-mds' once per process.
features.notes: Legacy upgrade helper.

features.name: MDSMap subscription and map handling
features.description: MDS subscribes to 'mdsmap'; the mon sends a standby-only map, the fs MDSMap, or an empty map, serving the MDS view only to an MDS-type session whose address vector equals the daemon's addrs; the MDS applies maps in order, validates compat (suicide if unwritable), respawns when removed, creates the MDSRank when a rank appears.
features.notes: MDS peers also push MMDSMap to each other before other messages.

features.name: Admin failover and sizing commands
features.description: mds fail, fs fail, fs set joinable/down/max_mds/allow_standby_replay/standby_count_wanted, mds repaired, fs reset, fs rm, fs new, fs compat, mds rm, mds rmfailed, mds freeze, mds set_state.
features.notes: Implemented entirely in the mon; the MDS only observes the resulting maps.

features.name: Orchestration helpers (ok-to-stop, last-seen, metadata, versions)
features.description: mds ok-to-stop checks degraded state and standby availability; mds last-seen uses in-memory FSMap history; mds metadata/versions/count-metadata read stored sys_info.
features.notes: Used by cephadm upgrade and the mgr.

features.name: Compat set gating
features.description: The daemon advertises get_compat_set_all(); the mon adds INLINE at boot and evicts on any later change; standby selection requires daemon compat writeable for the fs compat (and vice versa unless upgradeable); promote merges compat when upgradeable; the MDS suicides if a received map's compat is unwritable.
features.notes: Only mon-side mechanism that can keep incompatible MDS implementations out of a file system.

features.name: Mon-down and slow-election protections
features.description: Beacon stamps reset after a slow tick (> grace - interval) or leader change; replacement only if some MDS beaconed within max(interval, grace/2); laggy marking deferred up to mds_beacon_mon_down_grace while a mon is down or the quorum is new.
features.notes: Pure mon policy.

features.name: Quiesce DB leader and membership assignment
features.description: In encode_pending the mon sets qdb_cluster_members to all up:active ranked gids and qdb_cluster_leader to the lowest rank among them, for file systems modified in the epoch.
features.notes: Members are identified by gid; MDS uses monc->get_global_id() as its quiesce peer id.

features.name: Incarnation assignment
features.description: promote sets mds_info.inc to the FSMap epoch; the MDS tells the Objecter its incarnation; libcephfs treats an incarnation change with an address change as a restart.
features.notes: Kernel client detects restarts by address change.

features.name: MDS admin socket status/exit/respawn/lockup
features.description: status reports want_state, state, epochs, osdmap barrier; exit triggers suicide (DNE beacon); respawn execs; lockup sleeps holding mds_lock to test beacon suppression.

features.name: MDS feature bits in the boot beacon
features.description: The beacon's u64 mds_features (CEPH_FEATURES_SUPPORTED_DEFAULT) is stored in mds_info_t at boot only and not interpreted by the mon; MDS daemons AND the features of all up daemons (MDSMap::get_up_features) to choose encodings of journal events, inode stores, session maps and migration payloads.
features.notes: Only matters when several MDS implementations share a file system; a value that differs from the peers' changes their on-disk encodings.

serialization_points.name: Beacon::mutex
serialization_points.shared_state: Beacon epoch, want_state, seq_stamp, laggy, health metrics
serialization_points.why_serialized: Sender thread, ack dispatch, is_laggy() (called for every dispatched message) and mds_lock holders all touch beacon state; notify_health iterates all sessions while holding it and mds_lock, blocking beacon sends and ack processing.
serialization_points.notes: Metrics could be published as an immutable snapshot.

serialization_points.name: Heartbeat-gated beacon sending
serialization_points.shared_state: HeartbeatMap MDSRank handle reset under mds_lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: Liveness of the whole daemon is inferred from one handle that only mds_lock holders reset.
serialization_points.notes: Some liveness watchdog is required by the mon protocol; tying it to a global lock is not.

serialization_points.name: Laggy deferral of all dispatch
serialization_points.why_serialized: A daemon without beacon acks may have been replaced; it stops handling every message and replays them in order later.
serialization_points.notes: Self-fencing is needed, but read-only or shard-local work could be distinguished.

serialization_points.name: Shared messenger dispatch thread for beacon acks
serialization_points.why_serialized: Beacon acks are dispatched by the same thread that blocks on mds_lock for other messages.
serialization_points.notes: Long mds_lock holds delay ack processing and cause false self-laggy.

serialization_points.name: MDSMap application under mds_lock
serialization_points.shared_state: mdsmap pointer, rank state, peer epochs, recovery sets
serialization_points.why_serialized: Maps must be applied in order and state transitions validated against the previous map.
serialization_points.notes: Consumers mostly need an atomic snapshot of the newest map.

serialization_points.name: Rank phase transitions gated by mon round trip
serialization_points.why_serialized: Each phase boundary is a beacon, a Paxos commit and a map push; clients and peers act on the published state.
serialization_points.notes: Imposed by the unmodified mon and clients (reconnect at up:reconnect).

serialization_points.name: Atomic epoch and want_state update
serialization_points.why_serialized: A beacon with the new epoch and old state is an invalid transition and gets the daemon evicted.

serialization_points.name: Export target publication before migration
serialization_points.why_serialized: An export waits until the destination appears in the published export_targets (MMDSLoadTargets on tick, Paxos, map).
serialization_points.notes: Clients use export_targets; pre-publishing destinations avoids the wait.

serialization_points.name: Mon leader serial beacon processing
serialization_points.why_serialized: All beacons of all MDS daemons are processed by one leader under the monitor lock; every change is a Paxos proposal.

serialization_points.name: One rank grow/shrink at a time per file system
serialization_points.why_serialized: A creating, starting or stopping rank makes the map non-resizeable.
serialization_points.notes: Mon policy; adding N ranks takes N sequential rank bootstraps.

serialization_points.name: Health or state change bumps the MDSMap epoch
serialization_points.why_serialized: modify_daemon is called for every prepared beacon, so each change is broadcast to every MDS and client of the fs.
serialization_points.notes: Mon behaviour is fixed; the MDS controls how often health text changes.

serialization_points.name: Client eviction waits for blocklist
serialization_points.why_serialized: With wait=true the caller drops mds_lock and waits for the mon command and the latest OSDMap before killing the session.
serialization_points.notes: Fencing must complete before caps are reissued to others.

serialization_points.name: Tick-time target and health publication under mds_lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: update_targets and notify_health run in the timer callback holding mds_lock.

external_contract.detail: type 100, v8/compat 6, priority 196: paxos header(version=last seen epoch u64, -1 s16, 0 u64), fsid, u64 gid, u32 state, u64 seq, string name, s32 -1, string '', CompatSet, MDSHealth(ENCODE_START 1,1), sys_info map only when state==up:boot, u64 mds_features, s32 -1, bool false, string fs.
Session needs mon cap mds x; fsid must match; message source port must be nonzero; gid and name are taken from the payload; addrs from the connection.

version must equal the daemon's effective epoch (standby_epochs[gid] or its fs MDSMap epoch) for state/health to be processed; larger than the mon's committed epoch stalls the message in PaxosService::dispatch.

boot until standby seen; then report the mon-assigned state or request a legal successor; standby never changes state; standby-replay only damaged; invalid -> eviction with blocklist for rank holders.
Compat must not change after boot (compare != 0 -> fail_mds_gid); must contain incompat 7 INLINE because the mon inserts it at boot; must be writeable for the fs compat to be selected.
Leader must note a beacon at least every mds_beacon_grace (mon config, default 15 s); old-seq and repeated boot beacons do not count.
MMDSBeacon echoing gid, name, state and seq; sent after commit for prepared beacons, immediately for unchanged ones; never for compat eviction.
Null MMDSMap (epoch UINT32_MAX, no daemons) or a subscription map without the daemon; the MDS must stop serving.

Standby: single-entry map at standby epoch; ranked or standby-replay: full fs MDSMap; unknown: empty map at FSMap epoch; the MDS view is served only to an MDS-type session whose addrvec equals the daemon's addrs (otherwise the client view).
type 0x20a, paxos header, u64 gid, set<s32> targets; applied only for ranked gids; never acked.
type 90, map<s32 pool, vector<snapid>>; needs cap osd pool rmsnap; echoed back after commit to Octopus+ peers.
JSON {prefix: osd blocklist, blocklistop: add, addr: client addr} via MonClient; default mon expiry; result ignored.
JSON with confirm '--yes-i-am-really-a-mds'; sent once per process by the snap table server.
sys_info in the boot beacon: ceph_version, ceph_version_short, ceph_release, os, kernel_*, hostname, arch, mem_*, cpu, distro*, container keys, addr.

u16 mds_metric_t 1..17 map to codes MDS_TRIM..MDS_DUMMY (CACHE_OVERSIZED=11 precedes SLOW_METADATA_IO=12); unknown ids become '???'; id 0 (MDS_HEALTH_NULL) trips ceph_assert in MDSHealthMetric::decode and aborts the decoding mon; equality on type, sev, message.

external_contract.item: Blocklist fencing of failed rank holders
external_contract.detail: Every addr of the holder's addrvec blocklisted (TYPE_ANY, exact nonce) until now+mon_mds_blocklist_interval; same Paxos round as the FSMap change; a fenced MDS gets -EBLOCKLISTED.
Before replay the new holder waits until its OSDMap epoch >= MDSMap last_failure_osd_epoch.

Uses per-rank state (state<=0 entries skipped), addr (change -> close session, reconnect at up:reconnect), laggy_since (avoid laggy ranks, open sessions to their export targets), export_targets (reconnect targets in up:reconnect).

While mounting, requests fail with -EHOSTUNREACH (unless mount_wait) if the map is disabled, any rank damaged, m_num_laggy == m_num_active_mds, or no rank active. m_num_active_mds counts every mds_info entry including standby-replay, so with a standby-replay present the all-laggy test never fires and a laggy active still counts as active.

Address change -> mark down; reconnect when the rank is seen in up:reconnect; if the first map after the change shows the rank past up:reconnect while the previous state was before it (an incarnation change counts as NULL) the session is closed and caps are lost; ranks reaching active kick requests and connect to export targets.

Client::mount checks is_cluster_available only with require_mds: ceph-fuse passes fuse_require_active_mds (default true) and fails the mount on STUCK_UNAVAILABLE (any rank damaged, any up rank laggy, none in, none active); libcephfs ceph_mount passes false, so libcephfs/Ganesha mounts skip the check.
Tell commands skip laggy daemons; in-flight commands to gids that become laggy or disappear are cancelled with -ETIMEDOUT.
Mgr fetches 'mds metadata' for each FSMap daemon and refetches when metadata addr != stringify(info.addrs).
cephadm sets mds_join_fs=<service_id>, creates keys with mon 'profile mds', uses mds ok-to-stop, fs fail, fs set max_mds/allow_standby_replay and parses fs dump state strings such as up:active.
MDS_* health checks from beacons; mds fail/fs fail refuse without confirmation when MDS_TRIM or MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED is reported; fs set max_mds requires confirmation if any metric is reported.
status (want_state, state, epochs), exit, respawn, lockup.
u64 in the beacon, stored at boot in mds_info_t::mds_features; MDS peers use the AND over up daemons (get_up_features) for encodings.
osd blocklist add from evict_client carries no expire, so mon_osd_blocklist_default_expire (1 h) applies; MDS rank holders are blocklisted by the mon itself for mon_mds_blocklist_interval (1 day).

rust_implications.implication: Run the beacon sender and ack receiver on a path that never waits on shard locks or IO, but gate beacons on a watchdog that aggregates per-shard/worker progress; otherwise a wedged Rust MDS keeps beaconing and is never failed over (the mon only sees beacons). Decide explicitly whether one stuck shard silences the whole daemon.

The mon and clients only know rank states (replay, resolve, reconnect, rejoin, clientreplay, active, stopping). Per-subvolume shard recovery and parallel journal replay must happen inside these phases; clients reconnect per rank when the rank reaches up:reconnect. Requesting up:reconnect straight from up:replay is accepted by the mon whenever the daemon chooses.

Fencing is per daemon address vector and failover per rank; all subvolume shards hosted by one daemon share fate. Independent per-subvolume failover would need placement of subvolumes on different ranks (one daemon per rank) plus intra-cluster migration.

Advertise incompat {1..12} including 7 (INLINE) to satisfy mon checks; consider adding a private incompat feature id (13-63) so C++ MDS daemons are never selected for, and refuse to serve, a Rust-formatted file system (compat merges into the fs compat while the fs is upgradeable, e.g. at fs new).

Update (epoch, want_state) atomically, keep seq strictly increasing for the gid lifetime, report only epochs actually applied (never the null map's UINT32_MAX), use the MonClient global_id as gid and send beacons from the same address vector clients use.

Only the 17 known mds_metric_t ids produce meaningful health codes; per-subvolume SLA or QoS problems must be mapped to existing ids (e.g. MDS_SLOW_REQUEST with metadata) or reported via the mgr. Keep health message text stable, because every change bumps the fs MDSMap epoch and pushes a map to every client.

Read mds_beacon_grace/mds_beacon_interval from the mon config database so the daemon's self-laggy detection matches the mon's failure detection; support runtime changes of mds_join_fs (cephadm sets it).

Implement up:creating, up:starting, up:replay (wait for OSDMap >= last_failure_osd_epoch, or defensively the latest OSDMap), up:stopping/down:stopped, and at least an idle up:standby-replay, or document that allow_standby_replay must never be enabled.

Stop answering clients when beacon acks are missing for mds_beacon_grace and when removed from the map; a replaced Rust MDS must not keep granting caps or replying to synchronous Ganesha writes. Respawn equivalent must re-authenticate (new gid) and rebind with a new nonce because the old addresses are blocklisted.

If shards move between ranks, publish destinations with MMDSLoadTargets before migrating (kclient reconnects to export targets in up:reconnect and opens sessions to targets of laggy ranks; libcephfs connects to targets when ranks become active). Each new destination costs a mon round trip, so pre-publish stable targets.

Each additional rank is a separate daemon with its own gid and beacon; the mon adds or removes ranks strictly one at a time, and shrinking requires exporting everything from the stopping rank. Core-level parallelism must come from inside one rank.

Reporting down:damaged takes the whole rank offline (blocklist, clients see the fs unavailable) until 'mds repaired'; with per-subvolume shards prefer quarantining a shard internally and reporting MDS_DAMAGE via health metrics instead.
Do not route beacon acks through a queue shared with blocking metadata work; the C++ single dispatch thread causes false self-laggy detection when mds_lock is held.
Apply MDSMaps in epoch order and validate transitions with the same table the mon uses; publish the new map as an immutable snapshot to shards instead of processing it under a global lock.

Never emit a health metric with type 0 (the mon asserts on decode) and keep the compat masks bit-identical to the boot beacon (including INLINE); authenticate the mon session as an MDS entity from the same address vector the beacons and clients use.

open_questions: FSMap::erase sets last_failure_osd_epoch unconditionally (src/mds/FSMap.cc:1121). Code-reading path: in one check_health tick, laggy daemons are dropped in gid order; a rank holder (lower gid, blocklist epoch B, replacement promoted) followed by a laggy standby-replay of another rank of the same fs (higher gid, erase(gid, 0)) leaves last_failure_osd_epoch = 0, so the replacement's replay_start does not wait for OSDMap B. FSMap::stop (erase(sr, 0)) and 'mds rm' can do the same. Real-world impact untested.

MDSMonitor::prepare_beacon DAMAGED path calls MDSMap::get_gid(rank) (noexcept, up.at) for the reporter's rank; by code reading this terminates the leader if a standby-replay reports damaged while its rank is not up: between 'mds fail'/DNE/eviction of the holder and the next tick, with a frozen follower, or on a non-joinable fs. Not tested.
'mds set_state <standby gid> <n>' goes through FSMap::modify_daemon, which asserts info.state == STATE_STANDBY for standbys; by code reading this aborts the leader (hidden command; not tested).

pending_daemon_health is never reloaded from mds_health/<gid>; after a leader change the health gates for 'mds fail'/'fs fail'/'fs set max_mds' are blind until each daemon beacons again, and 'mds rm' leaves stale entries that has_any_health_warning still counts. Intended?

kclient m_num_active_mds counts all mds_info entries (including standby-replay) while m_num_laggy counts laggy 'in' ranks (linux/fs/ceph/mdsmap.c:163, 315-328), so the 'all laggy' availability test cannot fire when standby-replay daemons exist; confirmed by code reading, intent unknown.
The mon trusts the gid and name in the beacon payload (and the gid in MMDSLoadTargets) without cross-checking the cephx session (no check found in MDSMonitor); is any other layer enforcing this?

MDSHealthMetric::decode ceph_asserts type != 0, and the beacon is decoded by the receiving mon's messenger before any cap check, so a malformed beacon from any authenticated peer may abort that mon (code reading, not tested). A Rust MDS must never emit type 0.
